content:
Hello! I have a project in mind and i was wondering if it was of interest to merge into CSLib.

I've been reading this introduction to logical relations and i feel like the technique lends itself very well to Lean. I saw that the first example (STLC strong normalization) is essentially already in CSLib (there aren't a thousand ways to prove it). I was therefore planning on:

  1. Formalizing "another approach to type safety" as in the notes' third section, to contrast with the already existing STLC progress and preservation proofs.
  2. After that getting to Free theorems on SystemF, as that would be a reasonable next step and a fun result to have in the library

Does this sound reasonable and/or interesting to have in CSLib? I will probably start writing actual code towards the end of this week, in a private fork of CSLib, but I think it could be a good technique to upstream.
It may be interesting to connect this to Gluing using Synth Lean: e.g. https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol131-fscd2019/LIPIcs.FSCD.2019.25/LIPIcs.FSCD.2019.25.pdf
Yes, this work would be welcome. As you say we do have a version of strong normalization for STLC so we'll want to make sure not to duplicate this, but there's nothing for System F yet.

I'll try and tackle this in a satisfying way. I do believe that starting with type safety could be a good introduction/explanation of the technique in lean and also a way to get comfortable before tackling systemf, but i'll investigate and report back!
